title: Concurrency
theory:
## Concurrency in Go

Go has built-in support for concurrency with goroutines and channels.

### Goroutines

A goroutine is a lightweight thread managed by the Go runtime:

```go
go f()  // runs f concurrently
```

They start with minimal stack space and grow as needed.

### Channels

Channels are typed conduits for communication between goroutines:

```go
ch := make(chan int)    // unbuffered channel
ch := make(chan int, 3) // buffered channel with capacity 3
```

### Send and Receive

```go
ch <- value    // send value to channel
value := <-ch  // receive from channel
```

### Blocking

- Sending blocks until receiver is ready
- Receiving blocks until sender is ready

### Buffered Channels

Buffer lets send/receive proceed without blocking up to buffer size:
```go
ch := make(chan int, 2)
ch <- 1  // doesn't block
ch <- 2  // doesn't block
```

### Channel Directions

```go
func worker(in <-chan int, out chan<- int) {
    for n := range in {
        out <- n * 2
    }
}
```

### Select

Select lets you wait on multiple channel operations:

```go
select {
case n := <-ch1:
    fmt.Println("from ch1:", n)
case n := <-ch2:
    fmt.Println("from ch2:", n)
case <-time.After(time.Second):
    fmt.Println("timeout")
}
```

### Close

Close indicates no more values will be sent:
```go
close(ch)
for n := range ch {
    fmt.Println(n)
}
```

### sync.WaitGroup

Use to wait for multiple goroutines:
```go
var wg sync.WaitGroup
wg.Add(1)
go func() {
    defer wg.Done()
    // work
}()
wg.Wait()
```

exercises.title: Goroutine
exercises.description: Launch go sayHello(). Print main done. Use time.Sleep to let goroutine run.

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: Create ch := make(chan string). Send "ping" to ch in goroutine, receive and print.
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    ch := make(chan string)
    go func() { ch <- "ping" }()
    msg := <-ch
    fmt.Println(msg)
}

exercises.title: Buffered Channel
exercises.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 2. Send 10 and 20 without blocking. Then receive and print both.
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    ch := make(chan int, 2)
    ch <- 10
    ch <- 20
    fmt.Println(<-ch, <-ch)
}

exercises.title: Select Statement
exercises.description: Create two channels ch1 and ch2. Send to ch1 in goroutine after 10ms. Use select to receive whichever comes first.

exercises.title: Channel Close
exercises.description: Create channel, send 1,2,3 then close. Use range to receive until closed.
hints: for n := range ch prints until closed

exercises.title: Fan-In Pattern
exercises.description: Two goroutines each send one string on a shared channel; a third closes the channel after `WaitGroup` wait. Collect both messages, **sort them**, then print (receive order is not guaranteed).
hints: Use wg.Add(2) for the two sender goroutines
In a third goroutine, defer close(ch) after wg.Wait()
Range over ch to collect all values

exercises.title: WaitGroup
exercises.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch 3 goroutines that each print their number, then wait for all to complete before printing "done".
